correctness.rationale: Polar integration diagonalizes the Fock Toeplitz form. Integration by parts gives the endpoint exponential sum F, whose 2m-term Chebyshev zero count is proved by Rolle induction. Equality at r modal indices generates r-1 distinct F roots; hence r<=2m. The L1 monic minimizer exists by coercivity and has exactly 2m distinct positive simple zeros, because sign-orthogonality excludes fewer sign changes. Its negative intervals bisect the first 2m gamma moments, and the 2m-1 prescribed F zeros plus negative highest-exponent term force strict tail decay. Weighted-L1 minimizer uniqueness and reverse variational argument prove unique half-energy mask. The m=1,2 numerical checker corroborates the exact formulas but is not used to infer an infinite claim.

originality.rationale: The compared literature supplies radial Hermite/Fock eigenvalue integrals, single-annulus norm asymptotics, general symbol approximation, and nonlinear concentration foundations. None of the inspected complete relevant material gives the sharp 2m component-to-spectral-multiplicity theorem together with a unique exact half-energy construction for every m. The finite-exponential Rolle bound and L1 monic sign orthogonality are acknowledged classical tools, not themselves claimed as novel; their combined sharp radial inverse spectral design is the distinct result. Some historic quadrature sources and two recent manuscripts were not available in full, so historical-priority uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: The spectral degeneracy is controlled sharply by a natural geometric complexity invariant: the number of distinct annular components. The result holds for every number of components, every eigenvalue level, and all Hermite degrees; a unique half-energy construction attains the cutoff at the spectral norm. It gives a concrete inverse design tool for Gaussian short-time Fourier concentration and is not merely a numerical parameter slice or straightforward restatement of known diagonalization.
